Cregger's Resident Evil pulled in $108.3 (£93m) globally during its opening weekend, Deadline reported, split $60m in the US market and $48.3m internationally.
Cregger's Resident Evil pulled in $108.3 (£93m) globally during its opening weekend, Deadline reported, split $60m in the US market and $48.3m internationally.
That's more than Cregger's hit horror Weapons ($70m) and comfortably higher than any of the previous Resident Evil films.
It's apparently the second-best result for a horror film this year behind the sensation that was Backrooms ($118m).
Incidentally, the first Jovovich Resident Evil film, released in 2002, made $102.9m in total, Deadline noted, so Cregger's film has already beaten it.
2016's Resident Evil: The Final Chapter has a lifetime total of approximately $312m (half of that apparently coming from China).
That’s more than double Resident Evil: Afterlife, the franchise’s previous front-runner, which managed a $26 million opening in 2010 – not adjusted for inflation.
The new film did even better globally, taking $108.3 million internationally on a $75 million budget.
